name: NVIDIA Rubin Ultra
disclaimer: Roadmap product (H2 2027, announced at GTC 2025). Die and HBM footprints drawn to the same scale as other chips (1 unit = 4 mm; estimates where noted). Internal SM/Tensor Core structure is unannounced — this model reuses the Blackwell-style layout as a placeholder, clearly marked estimate. Heights, SM grids, DRAM layer counts, the die-to-die mesh and the substrate are illustrative.

components.name: Package substrate
components.desc: Multi-layer organic substrate for the 4-die Rubin Ultra GPU package. Roughly double the footprint of a 2-die Blackwell package to fit 4 reticle-sized dies and 16 HBM4E stacks.

components.name: Interposer (next-gen CoWoS)
components.desc: Advanced packaging carrying wiring between the 4 dies and 16 HBM4E stacks. NVIDIA has not disclosed the exact packaging technology for Rubin Ultra; assumed to be a CoWoS-L-class successor given the larger multi-die footprint.

specs.label: Packaging
specs.value: CoWoS-L class (assumed; exact process unannounced)

components.name: Die 0
components.desc: One of four reticle-sized compute dies in a single Rubin Ultra package — double the die count of Rubin/Blackwell's 2-die package. Software sees all 4 dies as one GPU.

specs.label: Compute dies (per package)
specs.value: 4 (announced; doubled from Rubin/Blackwell's 2)

specs.label: Process

specs.label: Die size
specs.value: ~26 × 33 mm (reticle-limited; assumed same physical limit as Blackwell)

components.name: Die-to-die mesh
components.desc: Fast coherent links across the 4 dies, extending Blackwell's NV-HBI concept to a 4-die mesh so CUDA sees one GPU. NVIDIA has not disclosed per-link bandwidth or exact topology for Rubin Ultra; link count and placement here are illustrative.

specs.label: Bandwidth
specs.value: Not officially disclosed for Rubin Ultra (Blackwell's NV-HBI was 10 TB/s)

components.name: L1 / Shared memory
components.desc: Programmable scratchpad shared by the threads of a block. Assumed to work like Blackwell's: TMA fills it with A/B tiles; Tensor Cores read operands straight from here. Rubin Ultra's actual SM microarchitecture is unannounced.

components.name: Tensor Core (generation unannounced)
components.desc: Multiplies matrix tiles; across all 4 dies the package reaches 100 PFLOPS dense FP4 (announced). Per-SM/per-core structure is assumed to follow Blackwell's 5th-gen Tensor Core design as a placeholder — the real Rubin Ultra Tensor Core generation is unannounced.

specs.label: Lowest precision
specs.value: FP4 (NVFP4, announced)

components.name: Register file
components.desc: Per-thread registers, assumed to carry over Blackwell's layout as a placeholder.

specs.label: Size (per SM, estimate)
specs.value: 256 KB (assumed, carried over from Blackwell)

components.name: Warp scheduler + scalar cores
components.desc: Each cycle picks a ready warp to issue; scalar cores run the epilogue. Assumed to carry over Blackwell's design as a placeholder.

components.name: TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator)
components.desc: Asynchronously copies tensor tiles between L2/HBM and shared memory. Assumed to carry over from Blackwell as a placeholder.

steps.text: 1. Weights W and activations X sit across 16 HBM4E stacks (1 TB announced) surrounding the 4-die package.
2. A memory controller reads the HBM group nearest its die.
3. Data needed by another die crosses the 4-die mesh — a scaled-up version of Blackwell's NV-HBI (link count/bandwidth not officially disclosed for Rubin Ultra).
4. Data lands in that die's L2 cache slice.
5. TMA copies A/B tiles from L2 into shared memory, asynchronously (Rubin SM internals unannounced; Blackwell structure reused as placeholder).
6. Tiles sit in shared memory, ready for the Tensor Cores.
7. Tensor Cores multiply the tiles, e.g. in FP4 — contributing to the package's 100 PFLOPS dense FP4 (announced).
8. Partial sums accumulate in Tensor Memory, not registers. Steps 5–8 repeat along K.
9. Epilogue: results move TMEM → registers; scalar cores add bias, apply activation, quantize.
10. Results go back to HBM4E; NVLink7 scales out across the NVL576 Kyber rack (576 GPU dies, 600 kW, announced for H2 2027).

summary.value: 4 reticle-sized dies in one package (announced; double Blackwell's 2)
~858 mm² per die (reticle limit, assumed same as Blackwell)
~34.7 PFLOPS FP8 per package (derived: NVL576 rack's 5 EFLOPS FP8 training / 144 packages)
~32 TB/s per package (estimate; derived from the NVL576 rack's 4.6 PB/s ÷ 144 packages)
~10,400 GB/s per package (derived: NVLink 7 rack total 1.5 PB/s / 144 packages)

scale.basis: Die ≈ 26 × 33 mm (reticle limit, assumed same physical limit as Blackwell); HBM4E stack ≈ 11 × 11 mm (estimate) — same basis as the B200 model so the 4-die/16-stack package reads at real relative size.
